_comment: Default theory (D = <W, Defaults>), Chapitre I-B.2. W is built per student by src/common.derive_facts(). Each entry is a Reiter default 'prerequisite : justification / conclusion'. Entries with an EMPTY justification list and type 'strict' are strict deduction rules encoded as defaults (alpha : / gamma): they are applicable in every extension. Literals prefixed with '~' are negations; a justification '~p' is consistent as long as p is NOT believed. D4a-c encode 'presume a normal interest when the questionnaire is missing'; D5a/D5b form a Nixon-diamond pair producing TWO extensions for tied profiles.

defaults.text: Normally, a student strong in algorithmics is suited for AI, provided nothing shows she dislikes AI and her mathematics are not critically weak.
Normally, a student strong in programming is suited for Software Engineering, unless there is evidence she dislikes it.
Normally, a student strong in networks & systems is suited for Cybersecurity, unless there is evidence she dislikes it.
If a student is suited for AI and her AI interest is UNKNOWN, presume by default that the interest is compatible and recommend AI (until proven otherwise).
For a student suited to both SE and Cybersecurity with equal declared interests: by default, orient towards Cybersecurity, as long as orienting towards SE is not already concluded.
Symmetric default: orient towards SE as long as orienting towards Cybersecurity is not already concluded. D5a and D5b conflict => two extensions for tied profiles (Nixon diamond pattern).
STRICT: suited for AI AND declared interest in AI => AI recommended.
STRICT: suited for AI AND strong problem solving => AI recommended.
STRICT: suited for SE AND declared interest in SE => SE recommended.
STRICT: suited for SE AND strong coding practice => SE recommended.
STRICT: suited for Cybersecurity AND declared interest => Cybersecurity recommended.
STRICT: suited for Cybersecurity AND strong problem solving => Cybersecurity recommended.
STRICT: average below 10/20 => the student needs academic remediation first.
